question_scores.question_text: When can I enroll in Medicare and select my coverage? And when can I make changes to my coverage after I've enrolled?
question_scores.response_text:
Here’s a clear breakdown of **when you can enroll in Medicare** and **when you can make changes after enrolling**:

---

## ✅ When You Can First Enroll in Medicare

### 1️⃣ Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)
This is your first chance to enroll.

- Starts: **3 months before** the month you turn 65  
- Includes: Your birthday month  
- Ends: **3 months after** your birthday month  
- Total: **7 months**

✅ You can enroll in:
- Medicare Part A (hospital)
- Medicare Part B (medical)
- Medicare Part D (drug coverage)
- Medicare Advantage (Part C)

⚠️ If you delay Part B or Part D without other qualifying coverage, you may face **late enrollment penalties**.

---

## ✅ If You’re Still Working at 65

If you (or your spouse) have employer coverage from active employment:

- You may delay Part B and Part D.
- You’ll get a **Special Enrollment Period (SEP)**:
  - You can enroll anytime while covered by the employer plan, or
  - Within **8 months** after employment or coverage ends (for Part B)
  - Within **63 days** after drug coverage ends (for Part D)

---

## ✅ Annual Opportunities to Make Changes

Once you’re enrolled, here are the main times you can change coverage:

---

### 🗓️ 1. Medicare Annual Open Enrollment
**October 15 – December 7 (every year)**

You can:
- Switch from Original Medicare to Medicare Advantage
- Switch from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare
- Change Medicare Advantage plans
- Join, drop, or change a Part D drug plan

Changes take effect **January 1**.

---

### 🗓️ 2. Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment
**January 1 – March 31**

If you're already in a Medicare Advantage plan, you can:
- Switch to a different Medicare Advantage plan, OR
- Drop Medicare Advantage and return to Original Medicare (and add Part D)

You can make **one change only** during this period.

---

## ✅ Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs)

You may qualify to make changes outside the normal windows if you:

- Move out of your plan’s service area
- Lose employer or other creditable coverage
- Qualify for Medicaid or Extra Help
- Move into or out of a nursing home
- Experience certain life events

---

## Quick Summary

| Situation | When You Can Act |
|------------|------------------|
| Turning 65 | 7-month Initial Enrollment Period |
| Each year | Oct 15 – Dec 7 |
| Already in Medicare Advantage | Jan 1 – Mar 31 |
| Special life event | Special Enrollment Period |

---

If you'd like, tell me:
- Your age
- Whether you're still working
- What coverage you currently have

And I can give you guidance specific to your situation.
